Long-press the orb to translate on-device (the language model downloads on first use). Add your own DashScope API key to translate through Alibaba Cloud Bailian (qwen3.7-flash) instead — better quality, and it falls back to on-device if the network fails.
Enter a new key to replace it
Not set. Leaving it empty = fully on-device, no cloud calls at all.
Add names, brands and jargon you say often (e.g. Atmos, Tonmeister) — recognition prefers these spellings.
Always replace what’s heard on the left with the word on the right (e.g. “pik” → “Pik”).
Every phrase you send from the keyboard stays on this phone. Tap to copy, swipe left to delete.
Slow network — used the on-device result

Sends automatically in %1$d s (%2$d-minute limit per recording)

Waits for your selected cleanup service, then inserts the final result once. Cloud failures get a separate attempt with a prepared local model. Cloud speech preference and field context are off by default; without an on-device Chinese speech pack, the system service is the fallback and a cloud hint appears.

Only affects Android’s system speech service (Google speech and the like) when it recognises over the network — where the audio goes is up to that service. This is separate from “recognise speech with this key” below, which is what uploads the whole recording to the service you choose. When off, a downloaded on-device Chinese pack is preferred; if unavailable, the system service still steps in and says so.

The whole recording goes to the service you choose (Groq / Gemini / Bailian) for re-recognition, and only replaces the system result if it succeeds. Failures, timeouts, bad length or no key fall back to the system recogniser. Audio leaves your phone. Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints don’t support this.
Cloud recognition returned nothing (see recent history for the reason). The keyboard still uses the system recogniser.
Microphone unavailable — allow recording access first.
Use surrounding text when refining (up to 500 characters)

When on, sends the current app name, that app’s tone (if you set one) and up to 500 characters before the cursor to the refining service you chose — only to work out what the transcript refers to and how formal it should be. It is never treated as transcript text and never sent anywhere else.
Use voice once in an app with field context on, then pick that app to set a usual tone. Settings stay on this phone; you still need the option above to send anything.
No apps recorded yet. Turn on field context above and use voice once in an app, then set its tone here.
For example: short and direct like a chat message; polite for email, no extra pleasantries.
Tone settings stay on this phone. Sending them still needs field context turned on above.

After downloading Google’s small Gemma 4 model (about %1$d MB, Wi-Fi only; allow roughly %2$s GB with the first-load cache), text is refined on your phone when no cloud key is set — nothing leaves the phone. With a key, the cloud service you pick below is still used. On-device refining takes a few seconds longer and fixes fewer jargon and typo cases.
Downloaded · preparing the model for the first time (about 1–2 min; refining starts once it’s ready)
Downloaded · model preparation failed (%1$s). Tap “Test On-device Refine” to retry.
Downloaded · first-time preparation needs about %1$d MB more space. Free some up, then tap “Test On-device Refine”.
Downloaded · used when no cloud key is set
Downloaded · a cloud key is set, so the cloud is used
Download didn’t finish (%1$s) — tap download again
Not enough space: needs about %1$s GB (model + cache). Free some up and tap again.
The downloaded file failed its checksum and was deleted — tap download again
This phone doesn’t have enough memory for on-device refining
Refining on device (the first run prepares the model, 1–2 min)…

1. Tap “Open Signup Page” below and sign in to Google AI Studio with your Google account.
2. Tap “Create API key”.
3. Copy the key it gives you, come back here, paste it and tap “Save”.
4. Tap “Test” to confirm it works.

1. Tap “Open Signup Page” below and sign in to GroqCloud with email or a Google account.
2. Tap “Create API Key” and give it a name.
3. Copy the key (shown only once), come back here, paste it and tap “Save”.
4. Tap “Test” to confirm it works.

1. Tap “Open Signup Page” below and sign in to the Anthropic Console (Claude’s developer dashboard).
2. Under “API Keys”, tap “Create Key” and give it a name.
3. Copy the key (shown only once), come back here, paste it and tap “Save”.
4. Tap “Test” to confirm it works.

1. Open the Alibaba Cloud Bailian console and activate model service (identity verification required).\n2. Create a key on the “API-KEY” page.\n3. Copy it, come back here, paste it, tap “Save”, then “Test”. (Same key as cloud translation below.)
1. Enter the endpoint URL and model name of any OpenAI-compatible service (e.g. your own server).\n2. Paste the key, tap “Save”, then “Test”.
Free, roughly a thousand requests a day. On the free tier Google may use submitted text to improve models; link a billing account in Google Cloud (you may not be charged) and it stops.
Free, roughly a thousand requests a day, and very fast; submitted data isn’t kept by default.

Billed by usage: add credit in the Anthropic Console or use your API credits; a Claude Pro/Max subscription can’t be used directly. By default Anthropic doesn’t train on API data. Claude can’t transcribe speech: cloud recognition uses your saved Groq/Gemini key instead.
New accounts get free credit, then you pay by usage.
Text goes to the endpoint you enter.
This key is out of free credit. Check your quota with the provider, switch providers, or tap “Remove” to run keyless.
The refined result didn’t pass review
Connection timed out — check your network.
The service answered, but the result doesn’t look like a refined version of the original, so it won’t be used.
嗯我們約禮拜三，不是，禮拜四下午三點在公司見，然後我搭到元山站以後再換車，悠悠卡記得先除值。
Enabled packs help recognition hear these words correctly. With Smart Refine on, misheard words (e.g. Jeman) also get corrected to the right spelling (Gemini).
One word per line; for a replacement write “heard→replace”
One word per line (e.g. Perplexity). For a replacement write “heard→replace” (e.g. cloud code→Claude Code). You can paste a word list exported from another keyboard, or one a friend shared.

This isn’t a UTUVO Type dictionary file.
This dictionary is from a newer UTUVO Type. Update first.

Share with iPhone and Mac: export, save to Google Drive or send it to yourself, then tap “Import Dictionary” on the other device. If both sides changed a word, the later one wins; deleted words stay deleted.
Haptics fire on press (not on release), and also on picking candidates and switching keyboards. Nothing fires when the phone is silent or the system has haptics off. Key clicks have their own switch.
Whether “繁” uses Zhuyin or Pinyin — tapping “繁” on the keyboard uses this. You can also switch inside the keyboard.
Do this once, and after that just tap the orb and talk.
Open Settings, search for “Keyboard”, and turn on UTUVO Type.
Open the UTUVO Type app once and tap “Allow” when the system asks for the microphone. Without it the keyboard can’t hear you.
Turn on UTUVO Type in keyboard settings, then tap any text field in any app and switch to it from the keyboard icon.
The orb sits in the middle of the keyboard. Tap once to record.
Tap the orb again to finish
Tap once more when you’re done and the text appears at the cursor.
“Send” on the right pastes the whole phrase; you can also edit it in the app first.
No setup needed each time: once the microphone and keyboard are enabled, tap the orb whenever you want to talk.
Hold the orb and the language arc appears — slide onto a language and release, and what you say next is translated into it.
Swipe left or right on the keyboard to move to the next language layer. You can also tap EN／繁／简 on the left.
Zhuyin or Pinyin on the “繁” layer
Choose Zhuyin or Pinyin under “繁” keyboard input in Settings; the 拼／注 key at the bottom switches on the spot too.
Keep holding to delete continuously; press and slide off to cancel that delete.
Select text → say how to change it

Select some text first — the orb turns lavender and says “Say how to change it”. Tap the orb, give the instruction out loud (e.g. “make it more formal”, “add coffee at the end”), then tap the orb again and the rewrite replaces your selection. Rewriting runs in the cloud, so it needs a key in Settings → Smart Refine (Groq / Gemini / Bailian / custom — whichever the engine badge shows).
Add names you say often to the personal dictionary
Names, brands and jargon you add get spelled that way when inserted, and cloud recognition and Smart Refine both use them.
Filler, corrections and punctuation are cleaned up before one final insertion. To use a cloud model, add your own key in Settings.
Cloud recognition (optional, needs your own key)

Save a key in Settings, then turn on “Cloud Recognition” — audio is recognised with your key for better results on jargon, and falls back to on-device if it fails. Audio leaves your phone, so skip it if that matters to you.
Check the microphone permission is allowed, UTUVO Type is enabled in keyboard settings, and the UTUVO Type keyboard is the one in use.
Open UTUVO Type to see the message; it’s usually the network or the key. Fix it and tap the orb again.
Can’t find or switch to the keyboard
Toggle the keyboard off and on again; sometimes you need to reopen the app after changing settings.

This deletes %1$d dictations past the limit. The usage numbers on the home tab are unaffected.
Delete every dictation? This can’t be undone. The usage numbers on the home tab are unaffected.
Raises the input gain and waits longer for silence so soft speech is recognised. The gain only applies to cloud recognition; the phone’s own recogniser only gets a more forgiving silence threshold.
Reorders Zhuyin whole-sentence candidates using the surrounding text; the model runs on your phone, offline.
When you talk through steps or key points, format them as 1. 2. 3.; off keeps paragraphs. Works best with Claude.
Use an HTTPS endpoint without credentials, key parameters or a fragment.
